Seven full cube enumerations provide independent finite spot checks; the universal proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: A cosine of a quadratic is the fundamental equal-weight sum of two inverse quadratic characters; its U3 norm is not a linear combination of the two individual unit norms. The exact signed-cube table reveals an arithmetic phase transition where interference can lower the eighth power even below the independent-term 1/128 benchmark, contrasting primes p=3 and p=5 and classifying every dimension. This is a motivated structural finite-field benchmark with a complete sign law, not an arbitrary small finite table; it does not purport to give a general higher-order inverse theorem.
